Branch layout (2026-09-05): on `rename/merry` / `feat/responsive-sessions` the iOS tree is still `ios/cmux/`, project `ios/cmux.xcodeproj`, target/scheme `cmux`, bundle id `dev.itsmaleen.cmux`, display name "merry". The full identifier rename (`ios/merry/`, `dev.itsmaleen.merry`) lives only in the locked worktree `worktree-rename-merry-full` (PR #30) and is not merged.

**Build (CLI):** since SwiftTerm was added as an SPM package (2026-09-05), build with the scheme, not the bare target — SPM package products only resolve through DerivedData, which a `-target` build never uses (`no such module 'SwiftTerm'`):

`cd ios && xcodebuild -project cmux.xcodeproj -scheme cmux -sdk iphonesimulator26.5 -configuration Debug build`

(The old `-target cmux` form still works for trees without SwiftTerm, e.g. `main`.) Product lands in DerivedData for scheme builds; `ios/scripts/screenshots.sh` locates it.

**SwiftTerm is pinned to `exactVersion: 1.18.0`** in `ios/project.yml`: 1.19+ adds `SwiftTermBuildInfoPlugin`, a build-tool plugin whose host tool gets built under `Debug-iphonesimulator/` while the plugin looks under `Debug/`, so every simulator build fails. Do not bump without re-checking.

**Logic tests:** `cd ios && ./scripts/run-tests.sh` (swiftc-compiled UIKit-free suites: text-search, scroll-follow, image-scaling, frame-fit).

**Screenshot tests:** `cd ios && ./scripts/screenshots.sh` builds, boots "iPhone 17 Pro" (udid C351D689-0865-4AB1-AAD2-83718721BB58), launches with `-UITestFixture frames -UITestFocus <surface>` and writes `ios/screenshots/*.png` (fails if a PNG is < 30 KB). Fixture mode seeds AppState from `ios/cmux/Fixtures/frames-*.ndjson` (recorded `herdr terminal session observe` frames) with no bridge. Portrait only: `simctl io screenshot` always captures the portrait framebuffer. Always Read the PNGs afterwards — the first pass looked fine by file size but was cropped to 47 columns.

**The Xcode project is generated by XcodeGen** (`ios/project.yml`; `xcodegen` at /opt/homebrew/bin). After adding/renaming files or touching project.yml: `cd ios && xcodegen generate`. `Info.plist` is generated too — on a merge conflict in pbxproj/Info.plist, take either side and regenerate.

One-time machine setup an agent did on 2026-09-05 (not repo state): `defaults write com.apple.dt.Xcode IDESkipPackagePluginFingerprintValidatation -bool YES` and `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`. The defaults key is only needed for SwiftTerm ≥ 1.19's plugin; with 1.18.0 pinned it can be reverted with `defaults delete com.apple.dt.Xcode IDESkipPackagePluginFingerprintValidatation`.

Watch disk space: booting a sim + install can exhaust the volume and then ALL Bash fails with ENOSPC. Clear with `rm -rf ios/build ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/*`, `go clean -cache`, `xcrun simctl shutdown all` and `xcrun simctl delete unavailable`. See [[feedback_build_verify]].

Makes every session render properly on the phone and scroll without jumping, and settles the mosh question. Based on `rename/merry` (#29); merge that first or retarget to `main` after it lands.

## Mosh: not implementing it
Full assessment in `plans/responsive-sessions.md`. Short version: mosh is a GPLv3 UDP transport with **no scrollback by design** (mosh issue #2, open since 2011) and no Swift/Go client. The Moshi app gets its history from herdr/tmux, not from mosh. What we take from it is the idea: the server owns the terminal state and streams rendered diffs to a real emulator on the client. herdr already produces exactly that stream, verified live.

## What changed
- **Scroll never jumps (phone).** `ScrollFollow.anchor` decides per update: follow bottom, keep offset on append, shift on prepend, keep distance-from-bottom on a repaint or card recomposition. Jump-to-bottom button gets a 44 pt target. Tests in `ios/scripts/test-scroll-follow.swift`.
- **opencode sessions read like Claude sessions, on both backends (bridge + phone).** New backend-agnostic transcript dispatcher (`bridge/internal/transcripts`) routes Claude → JSONL resolver, opencode → its SQLite store (ported from `worktree-opencode-sessions`). herdr supplies the session id directly. cmux never binds opencode, so the cmux backend proves a surface runs opencode by its tty, labels it in `surface.list` (`resume_binding {kind:"opencode", source:"bridge-tty"}`), and resolves the session by title + cwd. `agent.transcript` gains `agent_kind` / `session_title`.
- **Live terminal frames (bridge).** `surface.frames.subscribe/unsubscribe` + `surface.frame` / `surface.frames.ended` pushes, `capabilities.frames`. herdr implementation spawns `herdr terminal session observe` at the pane's native size (verified: it never resizes or disturbs the Mac pane), decodes NDJSON, and ends the stream with `backpressure` instead of ever dropping a delta; the observer's process group is killed on cancel. cmux answers `unsupported`. Tests: fake observer (full/delta/closed, 100 KB line, cancel, backpressure), multi routing, full WebSocket round trips.
- **Real emulator on the phone.** SwiftTerm (MIT, pinned 1.18.0 — see `project.yml` for why) renders the focused surface's frames: colours, cursor, exact layout, sub-second updates; font fitted to the card width; shell scrollback by dragging up. The view keeps the last full frame + deltas and replays them after every SwiftTerm geometry change (its `layoutSubviews` re-fits and crops the terminal otherwise). Surfaces without frames keep the polled text card. Frames bypass `@Published` (high frequency); only a feed's existence is published.
- **Screenshot tests.** `-UITestFixture frames` launch mode seeds the app from recorded herdr frames (`ios/cmux/Fixtures/*.ndjson`, no bridge); `ios/scripts/screenshots.sh` builds, boots the simulator, and captures `ios/screenshots/*.png`, failing on a missing/tiny PNG. Fixture decoding and font-fit math are covered by `test-frame-fit.swift`.
- **cmux parity (Phase D).** `plans/cmux-frames-proposal.md`: cmux already ships a full-frame+delta stream and a PTY byte tee for its own mobile app; the proposal exposes the same contract on the control socket (upstream issues #3003 / #11303 ask for it). Not posted upstream yet.

## Screenshots (recorded frames, iPhone 17 Pro simulator)
| Claude Code pane, 120×40 | Plain shell, 85×19 |
|---|---|
| ![claude](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsmaleen/merry/feat/responsive-sessions/ios/screenshots/claude-portrait.png) | ![shell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsmaleen/merry/feat/responsive-sessions/ios/screenshots/shell-portrait.png) |

## Verification
- `cd bridge && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` — green.
- Read-only live checks on this Mac: cmux `debug.terminals` labels all four open opencode surfaces and their conversations render; herdr observer streams `w2:p7` at its real 85×19 and closes 1 ms after cancel with no stray processes.
- End to end: a freshly built bridge on a spare port fronting the real herdr; a WebSocket client subscribed to a working Claude pane and received `capabilities.frames=true`, a 170×42 native grid, 1 full + 34 delta frames in 4 s; observer torn down on disconnect.

content.text:
PR #31 is open: https://github.com/itsmaleen/merry/pull/31 (`feat/responsive-sessions` into `rename/merry`, since #29 is still pending). Phase C and D are done to the point the loop asked for, so I'm ending the loop.

**What landed in the PR**

- **Live terminal frames for herdr.** The bridge relays `herdr terminal session observe` as `surface.frame` pushes with subscribe/unsubscribe commands and a `frames` capability. It observes at the pane's native size and never touches the Mac's pane. A slow phone ends the stream with `backpressure` and resubscribes for a fresh full frame rather than ever losing a delta.
- **A real emulator on the phone.** SwiftTerm renders the focused surface with colours, cursor, and exact layout. I found and fixed a bug in the agent's first pass: SwiftTerm's layout re-fits and crops the terminal, so both screenshots were cut at 47 columns. The view now replays the last full frame plus deltas after any geometry change, and the screenshots show the full 120 and 85 column panes.
- **Screenshot tests.** A launch-argument fixture mode seeds the app from recorded herdr frames with no bridge. The script in `ios/scripts/screenshots.sh` builds, boots the simulator, captures both panes, and fails on a missing or tiny PNG. The PNGs are committed and embedded in the PR.
- **cmux parity.** `plans/cmux-frames-proposal.md` is the upstream write-up. cmux already ships a full-frame-plus-delta stream and a PTY byte tee for its own first-party mobile app over a private transport, and issues #3003 and #11303 ask for the socket version. I did not post it upstream. Until it lands, cmux surfaces keep the polled text card.

**Verification**

- Go build, vet, and race tests are green, including fake-observer, multi-routing, and full WebSocket round-trip tests.
- End to end: a freshly built bridge on a spare port, fronting the real herdr, streamed a working Claude pane to a WebSocket client at its native 170x42 grid.
- iOS logic suites and the scheme build pass, and the screenshot script produced the two images in the PR.

**Things you should know**

- The iOS agent ran two one-time machine changes outside the repo: it set an Xcode default to skip package plugin fingerprint validation and downloaded the Metal toolchain. With SwiftTerm pinned to 1.18.0 the default is unnecessary and can be removed with `defaults delete com.apple.dt.Xcode IDESkipPackagePluginFingerprintValidatation`.
- Build the iOS app with `-scheme cmux` now; a bare `-target` build cannot resolve the SwiftTerm package.
- The card shows the emulator full-height with the history reader as a sheet. Putting history above the live screen in one scroll was not workable because SwiftTerm's view is itself a scroll view.
- A real-device run over Tailscale is still untested. The simulator pairing needed a tap on an iOS system dialog I could not automate.
